theme: Input repairs and data requirements for a common evaluation of proposed readings
question: Which input defects can we repair now, and what source, identity, exposure and calibration evidence is required before a common prospective comparison of readings?
outcome: Exact lexical lookup and written-form counting are implemented with explicit ambiguity and reviewed-variant records. On the same 162399 historical tokens, kā has 9 exact tokens against 22287 historical prefix matches; ā has 24 against 4458. All 24 proposed forms were audited: 8 unique exact entries, 15 homograph sets and 1 missing exact entry. Twenty-one generated input/preflight tests, independent count replay and three bench synthetic tasks pass. Ten blockers and a proposed participant contract identify the remaining work. No corrected rebus effect or new reading was evaluated.
challenge: Prefix frequencies and collapsed lexical fallback confounded the old features. Homographs, historical attestation, source-text boundaries and Winslow compound omissions require source judgments. Provisional physical identity and unreviewed exposure prevent a fresh confirmation claim. The shared harness has no calibrated rebus task.
remedy: Preserved old outputs, wrote a protocol before measuring the repair, separated written-form counts from sense selection, kept all dictionary derivatives local, implemented a fail-closed manifest preflight, and recorded explicit source and calibration gates.
retry_when: A source-adjudicated lexical inventory and general compound audit are available; the corrected features are integrated into a calibrated scorer with equal freedom for controls; and a reviewed object cohort has known identity and exposure before every participant freezes.

authors.model: GPT-6; exact backend identifier not exposed
